A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson says he delivered letter to Trump from Diddy from behind bars in bombshell claim as he opens up on friendship with disgraced rapper
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson says he delivered letter to Trump from Diddy from behind bars in bombshell claim as he opens up on friendship with disgraced rapper

Boxing legend Mike Tyson revealed that he hand delivered a letter from his friend Sean 'Diddy' Combs to President Donald Trump in a recent meeting.

In an appearance on SiriusXM radio show 'Andy Cohen Live,' the former fighter spoke at length about his friendship with the disgraced music mogul who is serving a 50-month prison sentence for a sex-crimes conviction.

Tyson said he is 'friendly with Puff' – using one of Combs' many stage names – before Cohen asked him if the boxer was 'surprised by what happened with him?'

'Listen, I was surprised that they went through so many lengths to get him,' the athlete replied.

'They used a 110-year-old rule to get him – that case 110 years ago, but they used it to get him. Can you imagine that?'

After being convicted on this charge, Tyson said that he spoke with Combs from jail – where he asked 'Iron Mike' to deliver a message to the President.

Mike Tyson says he was asked to deliver a letter from Diddy to President Donald Trump

Diddy - born Sean Combs - wrote Trump a letter from jail asking the President for a pardon

'And did you give a letter to the president from him?' Cohen inquired, to which Tyson replied: 'I did what he told me to do, yeah.'

In January, President Trump confirmed that he received a letter from Combs asking for a pardon. Trump did not reveal how he received the letter, but said that he wouldn't grant the request.

The '110-year-old' rule Tyson referred to was the 1910 Mann Act, a law that criminalizes the transporting of 'any woman or girl for the purpose of prostitution or debauchery, or for any other immoral purpose.'

Combs faced accusations of leading a criminal enterprise where he allegedly coerced victims to participate in debaucherous sex parties – nicknamed 'freak offs' – which occasionally involved travel across state lines and international borders.

After a two month trial, Combs was acquitted of trafficking and racketeering, a jury cited the Mann Act when finding him guilty of two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution.

Combs has denied all allegations of sexual misconduct and has attempted to appeal his conviction.

He is currently being held at FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey and still faces upwards of 70 civil lawsuits throughout the country.

In January, Trump said he got a letter from Combs but said he wouldn't pardon him

Combs is serving 50 months in prison on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution

Join the discussion Should celebrities be able to use their connections to seek pardons for serious crimes?

Combs' release date has moved multiple times since his incarceration due to his alleged misdeeds behind bars.

An NBC News report revealed it was pushed back from January 21, 2028 to March 2, 2028 after he allegedly made fellow inmates cook and clean for him, give him massages and received access to outside alcohol and a cellphone.

In an August 2025 interview, Trump addressed Combs' conviction in an interview with Newsmax.

'I was very friendly with him. I got along with him great,' the President said at the time.

'[He] seemed like a nice guy,' Trump continued. 'I didn't know him well, but when I ran for office he was very hostile.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua braced for dramatic 1am start time under new proposal to Cardiff Council - and the Gypsy King wants to walk out flanked by Donald Trump!
Sports.content:
The highly-anticipated bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could be set for a 1am start time at the Principality Stadium, Cardiff, in December.

That's after Cardiff Council received an application stating the ring walks are planned to start gone midnight, with proposals for the stadium to stay open until 3.30am.

According to the BBC, Millennium Stadium Plc has applied to change its premises licence to allow the fight to take place late 'on a very limited one-off occasion'.

Fury has suggested he will try to persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk. 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available. Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

There is also a request to play live music until 3am on the same date, with a live performance expected before the ring walks.

It is proposed that the stadium roof is closed for the duration of the event, with enhanced security in place.

Other authorities and members of the public can make an objection until November 3, and a council hearing will be held to consider them. It is understood the permission will be granted if there are no objections.

There is a proposal for the ring walks for Tyson Fury (left) vs Anthony Joshua (right) to take place at 1am

There was initially doubt over whether the fight would take place in the United Kingdom or New York City.

It is understood Eddie Hearn pushed hard for the fight to be in Cardiff, with broadcaster Netflix keen to host it later so it can be shown at a reasonable time in the States.

Fury is currently favourite to take victory in the bout, with the Gypsy King claiming he has battled back from 28st – as heavy as an adult mountain gorilla – to chisel down to the shape he's in today.

Fury's physique has fluctuated heavily down the years – in January he described himself as a 'fat, binge-drinking junk-food addict' as he returned from retirement for a fifth time – but he is not messing around on this occasion.

Each fighter will pocket £75million from the face-off. As Daily Mail Sport revealed in September, the two fighters would have been taxed around 30 per cent of their purses in America, compared to 20 per cent in the UK, with Joshua particularly unhappy about the prospect of an extra £7.5million being added to his bill.

The two-time world champion instead demanded that his contract be honoured, which stipulated a British-based fight.

Hearn initially pushed for Wembley Stadium, but the combination of a roof over the Principality Stadium and the Welsh government’s willingness to bend their late-night curfew swung the fight towards Cardiff.

Sports.title: Dana White labels Eddie Hearn a NEPO BABY as war of words escalates between the promoters over Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua showdown
Sports.content:
Dana White's war of words with Eddie Hearn has taken another turn after the UFC and Zuffa Boxing chief essentially branded his rival a nepo baby.

The duo have been at each other's throats over various topics this year, from Conor Benn's future to the £150million blockbuster fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Things have escalated over the last month. White, who runs Zuffa Boxing alongside Saudi Arabia's boxing supremo Turki Al-Sheikh, has been billed as the main promoter for the heavyweight showdown and fought for the contest to take place in New York City.

Hearn, who successfully wrestled the fight back to Cardiff, has claimed that the contract Joshua signed stipulates that White cannot be involved in the contest and threatened crunch talks with broadcaster Netflix over White's attendance at Fury and Joshua's press conference on Wednesday in London.

And now, White has taken aim. He said on the Diary of a CEO podcast: 'Eddie's not the guy, Eddie's dad is the guy.

'And I'm not saying this to s*** on Eddie - I'm just being honest. I don't dislike Eddie. But he's not the guy; his dad's the guy.'

Dana White (left) has taken aim at Eddie Hearn (right) as their war of words continues - source: X - @danawhite

White branded Hearn a nep baby due to the sporting success of his father Barry (second left)

Barry Hearn, Eddie's father, has been a sports promoter since the 1970s and has had a huge influence on the likes of boxing, darts and snooker.

Eddie, though, now works in his own right though, according to White, is in his dad's shadow.

White continued: 'Frank Warren's the real guy. I just saw this interview with him; I was like, 'F***ing love it… all this f***ing talking and all this f***ing bulls***, let's f***ing fight.''

There had been doubt over whether the December 11 fight would in fact go ahead due to the involvement of White.

White, whose involvement has been criticised by sections of the British boxing public, was grilled by the media in a cagey press conference, where he labelled the bout a 's***show' while conceding he has 'no idea' if the contest will take place.

'I don't know. The guy who is supposed to be helping the fight has been hurting the fight the entire time,' he said. 'He hasn't done the fight any favours. I don't know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.'

When asked whether he would step aside to allow the fight to go ahead, White said: 'That's not up to me. I'm involved in the f***ing fight.

'If Eddie Hearn really cared about this f***ing fight — first of all the fight would've happened a f***ing long time ago, one. Number two, he could finance the thing himself.

'Listen, this whole thing's a s***show right now. We'll all know a lot more in the next three, four days, see how this thing plays out.'

The duo have been at a battle over who will promote the fight between Tyson Fury (left) and Anthony Joshua (right)

White had initially raised eyebrows when Benn left Hearn's Matchroom to join Zuffa.

It remains to be seen whether White will have any involvement.

Hearn said this weekend: 'At this point, (White's) completely cooked. What he actually said was, "We're doing the TV production". Which, again, in the contract, is prohibited.

'After that video (of White saying he was producing the fight), I spoke to Sela (the Saudi entertainment company listed as promoters of the event). I said, "Have you seen this video?" They said, in writing, "Yes, and it's completely untrue".

'(White) cannot do that under the contract. They want me to meet them in LA next week, which I probably will.'

Sports.title: From beauty to beast! Former 'Miss Germany' targets a BOXING career and is set for her professional debut
Sports.content:
A former winner of Miss Germany has announced a surprise career switch - and will swap the catwalk for the boxing ring at the age of 33.

Tatjana Genrich was voted Germany's most beautiful woman in 2022 and has now announced she will make her professional boxing debut next month in Magdeburg, rekindling her childhood love of the sport.

Genrich was the Saxony-Anhalt state champion in the flyweight division for amateur boxers between 2007 and 2009. And she recently opened up on why she originally went into the sport, saying: 'At school I was often bullied and I wanted to find a way to defend myself. That's how it all started.'

This then led to her attending a sports school in Halle, Germany where she was picked up by boxing promoter Ulf Steinforth. Years later he reconnected with the model after her fame and stature had grown and suggested the former amateur champion try her hand in the professional ranks.

When asked about their talks, Genrich said: 'Since I sponsor the ring girls at his boxing events, he approached me one day and asked if I wouldn't like to get back in the ring. I finally agreed and am now about to make my professional debut.'

Only four years ago she was Miss Germany... now Tatjana Genrich has her sights set on a career in boxing

The supermodel turned boxer still posts regularly to her 44,500 Instagram followers and owns her own modelling agency

Genrich will be hoping to her journey will inspire a new generation of young women into different sports

Promoter SES Boxing are backing Genrich to become the country's next big superstar, saying: 'Tatjana can follow in Regina Halmich's footsteps. She has all the necessary qualities, an incredible presence, and is extremely ambitious.'

Halmich won 54 of her 56 fights during a storied career between 1994 and 2017 which saw her become one of the most successful female boxers of all time, and also modelled for German magazines.

To prepare for her first fight on November 14, Genrich - who also runs her own modelling agency with 80 models under contract - has begun a rigorous training routine that sees her spending five full days a week in the gym.

In her corner she will have coach Dirk Dzemski, who guided Robert Stieglitz to world champion status in the 2010s.

Genrich also detailed another motivation to succeed in her new career, saying:' I want to be a role model for young women and show them that you can be successful in both your career and sports.

'I train in areas like posture, running and choreography. This prepares me for competitions as well as events like fashion shows.'

Sports.title: Tyson Fury plans to invite 'old buddy' Donald Trump to be part of his ringwalk for £150m mega-fight with Anthony Joshua: 'I'll definitely make the offer!'
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has suggested he will try and persuade United States president Donald Trump to join him for his ringwalk when he takes on Anthony Joshua in December.

Fury met the president at the UFC Freedom 250 event at the White House in June, joining Trump, First Lady Melania Trump and a host of MAGA royalty on the South Lawn.

He raised eyebrows with a cap, which featured a particularly bold message of support for Trump. 'Donald Trump for Prime Minister', it read alongside an embroidered British flag.

The slogan was a nod to Trump's signature red 'Make America Great Again' caps, which he sported throughout his election campaigns.

It was there Fury said he was keen to take on Joshua in the near future – and that fight has come to fruition, and will take place on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

And Fury is keen to have his friend there. He said: 'I'll definitely make that offer to my old buddy, old pal, and we'll see if he's available.

'Probably unlikely because of the situation he's in at the moment, being the President of the United States.'

Tyson Fury (centre) has said he will ask Donald Trump (right) to join his ringwalk when he faces Anthony Joshua

Though Fury may want Trump in his corner, Joshua will literally have a Fury in his, with Tyson's uncle, Peter, part of Joshua's group of trainers.

Tyson shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years, but his father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives'.

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

Sports.title: John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown
Sports.content:
John Fury hits out at brother Peter, calling him a 'cockroach' for joining Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of Cardiff showdown

John Fury called out his brother Peter for being a 'cockroach' after his estranged brother joined Anthony Joshua's camp ahead of the Briton's showdown with his son Tyson in December.

The long-awaited Battle of Britain is set to take place in Cardiff after months of back-and-forth between the Fury and Joshua camps, but neither John nor Peter will be in the corner of the Gypsy King, after Joshua announced this week that Fury's uncle had helped with his preparations.

Eyebrows were raised due to Peter's family ties, but Fury shrugged off suggestions that Joshua would have the inside track claiming that he hadn't spoken to him in years.

His father John was even more emphatic in discussion with Playbook Boxing, hinting at a betrayal from his brother which meant that he will 'never speak to him as long as (he) lives.'

'If he was to do that (talk to Joshua) in any way, shape or form, that would make him the lowest form of human being,' John stressed. 'Even thinking about doing it, that makes him the biggest dog, the biggest untrustworthy dog of all time.

'If he's going to start giving phone calls and advice, meeting in secret, giving him secret sessions, he's a f***ing cockroach.

John Fury called out his brother Peter (left) for potentially helping Tyson's rival Anthony Joshua ahead of their Cardiff showdown (pictured in 2015)

'The only advice he could have wanted is on Tyson, isn't it? There is no smoke without fire.'

As if speaking directly to Peter, he finished: 'Son, give your head a wobble. Don't sell your soul to the devil for a fiver.'

Peter shared on social media that he had spoken to AJ 'two months ago' about 'advice on his skill set', calling the Londoner 'a really nice guy'.

'After his fight anything he needs from me (would) be a pleasure. He has a great team around him (including) Team Usyk.'

John may have been staunchly defensive of Fury in the context of Peter doing anything to sabotage him in the ring, but relations between father and son remain minimal after having been, in John's words, 'completely destroyed'.

The duo are at loggerheads over Fury Junior's career, with his father adamant that he should prioritise his health and wellbeing by retiring for good after two failed attempts.

Peter previously trained Fury between 2011 and 2017, but left the camp amid a schism with father and son.

The Gypsy King had previously sought to set the record straight on Peter's involvement with his rival on social media, deeming Joshua's comments 'categorically untrue'.

'Even if Peter Fury hated me, he’s still my family,' he said. 'That would mean he would be a Fredo, scorpion, snake, rat, b****** piece of s*** if he did that.'

Sports.title: Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh calls out Dua Lipa in bizarre rant about pop sensation during Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference
Sports.content:
Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh calls out Dua Lipa in bizarre rant about pop sensation during Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference

Boxing chief Turki Alalshikh has claimed that Dua Lipa has refused to perform at the Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua super-fight in a bizarre tirade against the pop sensation during the launch press conference.

On Wednesday evening, Britain's two most iconic boxers of the last two decades went face to face for the first time since their eagerly anticipated clash was announced last week.

Ahead of the press conference, Alalshikh, who was lauded by Fury, Joshua and many others during the evening for financing the fight, was invited to speak about how the 'Battle of Britain' came to be.

New York's Madison Square Garden and Wembley had previously been billed as potential venues for the 'super' heavyweight clash, but it has since been confirmed that the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales, will host the contest.

During his explanation of how the venue was eventually decided, Alalshikh took a swipe at Dua Lipa in the process.

He said: 'I will be honest today, I know that London wouldn't give me the stadium until 2am, and I know that Dua Lipa will not perform in the stadium, because she doesn't like boxing, and maybe she doesn't like me.'

Turki Alalshikh went on a bizarre tirade during Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua press conference

The boxing chief claimed that Dua Lipa has turned down the chance to perform ahead of the long-awaited bout

Dua Lipa's representatives have been approached for comment by Daily Mail Sport.

Alalshikh went on to also explain the financial losses that staging the bout in Britain has led to.

He added: 'Nobody questioned me about UK. I love the British people, I try to deliver everything for them. Put yourself in my shoes; there's a situation to lose $70million (£52.8m); the best is to have it in a good time zone.

'I have two reasons, and I know London won't deliver it; they won't give me the stadium until 2am... Wales delivered it; it's still the UK, the town of Ryan Giggs, let's do it.'

Anthony Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been vocal about his and the two-time heavyweight world champion's desire to have the fight staged in the UK.

The chairman of Matchroom took his moment on stage at the British Airways ARC to thank the British boxing community for applying the 'pressure' to ensure the fight is played out on British soil.

Fury and Joshua faced off for the first time ahead of their super fight on Wednesday evening

'I'm excited,' Hearn said. 'Turki, I know we've fallen out, but I promise you this'll be the greatest night you've ever had in boxing.

'On a serious note, when we talked about this fight, you envisaged it for British boxing. This guy (Joshua) has changed boxing in this country. So has Tyson Fury. We are the envy of the boxing world.

'We can't stage it anywhere else. Thank you to the British public for putting the pressure on. We couldn't do it, we failed.'

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton left £30MILLION estate after his tragic death, new figures reveal, as son Campbell claims family are 'completely in the dark' amid dispute over late boxer's finances
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton reportedly amassed a £30million fortune before his death last year, though uncertainty remains over how the boxing legend's estate will be distributed.

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business empire worth more than £20million, with at least another £10m tied up in property investments, according to The Sun.

Trustees were appointed to manage Hatton's estate after he took his own life in September last year.

However, sources close to the family claim communication with the trustees has since broken down, with one describing the situation as a 'complete mess', according to an earlier report in The Sun.

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25, and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12. However, a year after his death, the family are still waiting to learn how and when the estate will be distributed.

Campbell told The Sun on Wednesday: 'My family is still completely in the dark. We’ve had no involvement in my dad’s finances for over 15 years.'

Hatton, who died aged 46 last September, won multiple world titles before using his fight earnings to build a business and property empire

It was thought Hatton had intended for his fortune to pass to his three children, Campbell, 25 (above), and daughters Millie, 14, and Fearne, 12

During his successful boxing career, Hatton used his fight earnings to finance a string of businesses, many of them linked to property investments in his hometown of Hyde, as well as in Leicestershire, London and Kent.

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'.

'Everyone who knew and loved Ricky would give anything to have him back. But during his life he's done a great job of providing for the people he loved the most, his children,' the source added.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price.

The house, where Hatton was found in September last year, was put up for sale shortly before his death for £1.85million but was later taken off the market following his tragic death.

The mansion then went back on offer for £1.75million, then £1.65million before it was sold for £1.5million.

It was described by the estate agent as being a 'landmark modern residence offering luxury, space and unrivalled lifestyle features'.

It said that the five-bedroom six-bathroom property, which was built in 2010, had been 'impeccably designed'.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail reported that Hatton's house had been sold for £1.5m this year after £350,000 was knocked off the original asking price

One source said Hatton was 'determined to ensure that he had a financial legacy from his incredible career'

Hatton put his own stamp on the property, decorating it with personal touches including a traditional telephone box in the garden and an array of Manchester City memorabilia. Among its more unusual features are seats salvaged from the club's former Maine Road stadium.

It has extensive landscaped grounds with greenbelt views, plus a leisure suite with a heated indoor pool and jacuzzi.

A private gym and cinema room complement a games room and bar area, which is separated from the pool by a striking glass wall.

The principal bedroom suite features a walk-in dressing room, a luxurious en suite bathroom, a crushed-velvet chaise longue and dark patterned wallpaper.

Elsewhere, the property offers multiple reception rooms and expansive open-plan living areas centred around a high-specification, dark-panelled kitchen.

Situated in the sought-after area of Gee Cross in Greater Manchester, the estate is equipped with advanced security features, including CCTV.

The estate agents said: 'This is a rare opportunity to acquire a truly outstanding home in one of the North West's most prestigious and sought-after residential locations.'

For confidential support, call Samaritans on 116 123, visit samaritans.org or visit thecalmzone.net/get-support.

Sports.title: McLaren targets Norris’ costly fuel system issue with Singapore F1 power unit fixes
Sports.content:
The McLaren F1 team has made a number of peripheral changes to Lando Norris' Mercedes power unit in a bid to eradicate a persistent fuel system problem.

McLaren was left significantly off the pace on Baku's long straights two weeks ago compared to Mercedes, with which it shares engines. But while some of its deficit was explained by intrinsic car weaknesses and by how it ran the Mercedes unit, Norris' car was particularly down on top speed in qualifying with what McLaren identified as a fuel injection issue. The issue returned intermittently in the race, also on Oscar Piastri's car to a lesser extent, and then hampered the team in last weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

It's understood McLaren has now decided to make a number of changes to auxiliary components related to the power unit, including the fuel system, which is on the team side rather than Mercedes, ahead of Singapore FP1 in a bid to resolve the issue.

"[I am] hopeful. We need to get on track first and see how much better it is," Norris said on Thursday.

"'It's been a frustrating two weekends trying to figure out what the issue has been and why there's just been a constant lack of straight-line speed and performance. And especially in this kind of battle we've been in, the last two qualifying [sessions] it's been two or three positions. So, it's cost me quite a lot."

Photo by: Liam Fabre

Singapore is one of the least power-sensitive circuits on the F1 calendar, but with a close battle between the top four expected, McLaren can't leave any performance on the table, and FP1 is a good opportunity to see if its fuel system issues are a thing of the past.

"It's obviously also a circuit where straights are not the highest priority and not as detrimental as the last few weekends," the reigning world champion said. "But nevertheless, you always want to go down the straights as quick as you should be able to and it's always tough when you come out of corners better and end up going slower.

"At the same time, there's obviously things I can do better as well. But confident that the team has done a good job. They put a lot of work into trying to figure out things and I'm hopeful that it'll be better this weekend. But honestly, I have to get out on track and see first."

More generally, Singapore is an important test for McLaren to verify whether its puzzling lack of performance in Malaysia was a one-off. The Sepang circuit was expected to suit the MCL40's strengths, but instead McLaren was only the fourth-fastest team on the circuit, potentially linked to how the car's aerodynamics interacted with the extremely rough track surface.

Sports.title: Audi F1 drivers reveal biggest engine limitation – and why they’re not worried
Sports.content:
In theory, the Marina Bay Street Circuit in Singapore should suit Audi well. The team led by Allan McNish would normally benefit from tracks on the Formula 1 calendar that are slightly less power-sensitive, but that rule of thumb does not necessarily apply in Asia.

Yes, in terms of outright power, the gap to the leading engine manufacturers should be smaller, but according to the drivers, another factor is causing Audi problems in the extreme conditions of Malaysia and Singapore.

“I think we have to be cautious and careful”, Nico Hulkenberg said during his Thursday media session.

“I think Malaysia brought some new things to light and these climatic conditions are not so favourable for our PU at the moment. We definitely had some struggles on that side and obviously here it's more of the same.”

Just as in Malaysia, the FIA has issued a so-called heat hazard declaration for the Singapore Grand Prix, indicating that temperatures of 31 degrees Celsius or higher are forecast. Hulkenberg therefore expects another challenging weekend.

“It is a less power-sensitive circuit on paper, for sure, but my personal expectations are not too high for the moment”, the German said.

Asked whether this is mainly related to cooling – with Audi having to open up more of the bodywork and consequently losing aerodynamic performance – Hulkenberg clarified that this is not the case.

Nico Hulkenberg, Audi Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

“No, I think we suffer from power.”

This means that Audi is losing outright engine power in the extreme heat, an assessment shared by team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto.

“Yes, I would say that right now, especially in the last races, it’s our biggest limitation”, Bortoleto said when asked about the heat by Autosport.

“I think what we already have for our first season is something decent. We just need to make some more steps to improve drivability, the situations of the climatisation that you were mentioning, and yeah, that's it.”

However, Bortoleto is fully confident that Audi will take those steps and eventually become the benchmark in terms of engine performance in F1. The Brazilian draws that confidence partly from Audi's successes in DTM and the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

“If I trust them? Absolutely. I think they can fix it. These people in Neuburg have built the best engines in other series that they have taken part in in the past, and I have no doubts they're going to do the same in Formula 1.

“We just need to give them time. We cannot believe that we would arrive in Formula 1 in the first year and build the best thing ever made. It would make the others look like... I would swear right now, but you understood what I was going to say!

“So we need to have patience. I believe in the people that are there in Neuburg, and I believe they're going to make something great.”

Audi finds answers about its major upgrade package

Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

While there are still areas for improvement on the power unit side, the German-Swiss team has now found answers regarding the major upgrade package it introduced in Baku.

The Baku City Circuit predominantly featured 90-degree corners and therefore did not provide a representative picture, but after back-to-back tests in Malaysia, it is clear that the upgrade has indeed been a step forward.

“Well, we concluded that it worked. It worked pretty OK, like we expected”, Bortoleto said.

“Entry, mid, exit of all the corners, I think we made a good step everywhere. There were a lot of doubts after Baku, because we had a tough weekend, about the package and if it worked or not. But I think now we can finally put a dot on this and say that we are sure that it worked as expected and that things are working in the right way.”

It also underlines that F1 teams often need some time to fully understand major upgrade packages and extract the maximum performance from them. In Audi's case, that has now happened, as Hulkenberg also confirmed when asked by Autosport.

“Yes, we are for sure closer [to understanding it]. The understanding obviously grows and builds with every session you do. You do different setup variations, you scan the delta to map, and in general you build your correlation between the track, the wind tunnel and CFD, so it's good.

“I think there's probably still some bits and bobs to explore and to discover, but it's not like we're going to get another second out of it or something.”

Sports.title: FIA completes investigation into F1 chaos in Malaysia and announces measures
Sports.content:
Ahead of the Singapore Grand Prix, the FIA has issued a statement following the events at Sepang. The opening phase of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia descended into chaos when half the field came to a standstill behind the safety car.

The issue turned out to be a software bug linked to the 250kW restrictions imposed by the FIA for wet-weather races. Nikolas Tombazis immediately provided an explanation to the media after the race, but added that the FIA would conduct a more in-depth investigation in the following days.

That investigation has now been completed, with the FIA focusing on four crucial areas.

First, the specific cause has been identified, with the FIA explaining:“The review concluded that some cars running on low engine RPM in certain circuit sectors where a 250kW power reduction was applied experienced a loss of power beyond the original intent and that could not be recovered in those sectors.”

A software bug caused the electric motors to go into lock-down mode in the slowest parts of the circuit. With no electric power available to offset the turbo lag, nothing happened when the drivers pressed the throttle pedal.

The FIA subsequently intervened with a rapid software update, which was sent to all teams and manufacturers to install ahead of the restart. The emergency solution was to lift the restrictions associated with the 250kW limit in certain minisectors where the problem occurred.

The same temporary solution will be used in Singapore if similar weather conditions are expected, the FIA has confirmed.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

“As a result, the configuration established for the Sepang event will be reinstated for the Singapore Grand Prix should similar weather conditions be expected. Additionally, a further update to the wet weather software will be released for the United States Grand Prix on October 25.”

This means the solution will come in two stages: a repeat of the emergency fix this race weekend, followed by a more permanent update to the wet-weather software ahead of the race in Austin.

Tombazis already confirmed on Sunday that the specific problem encountered in Malaysia would not happen again, although he could not guarantee that no new bugs would emerge with the extremely complex 2026 power units.

“Obviously, that was a major criticality and we need to make sure we avoid it. But can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no. But we will do our best to avoid it, of course”, Tombazis said.

The FIA's single-seater director also indicated that the software had not been tested sufficiently due to the lack of wet-weather running in 2026, which meant the FIA was unable to prevent the problem.

However, the governing body has now clarified that the software was indeed tested during the opening practice sessions for the Belgian and Dutch Grands Prix, but that the issue did not surface on those occasions.

Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

Logically, that is because the cars were completing laps at normal speeds during those runs and did not reach the extremely low speeds encountered behind the safety car in Malaysia.

For precisely that reason, the FIA will also work with teams and manufacturers to explore ways of improving the software testing process, according to the statement.

“The review also recommended that measures would be implemented for testing of the software, recognising that opportunities for testing are limited, to make it robust as possible.

“The FIA, together with the teams and Power Unit Manufacturers (PUMs), will continue to strengthen Power Unit software testing and verification capabilities, enhancing the overall validation process through independent assessment and collaborative feedback, including input from the supplier of the standardised Electronics Control Unit (ECU).”

Sports.title: Inside Alonso's decision to contest the 2027 Dakar Rally with Aston Martin
Sports.content:
Great speculation has accompanied Fernando Alonso in recent months as he held back on confirming his future in Formula 1. Now it appears that not only has he been able to agree favourable terms with Aston Martin to stay on in F1 for 2027, but also persuaded the car manufacturer to back him in another assault on the Dakar Rally, Autosport understands.

The deal was agreed as far back as August but has only just been leaked via the Spanish media. During the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, Alonso made some cryptic remarks about "surprises" that could emerge "in the next few weeks". This was assumed by many to mean some kind of GT racing entry with Max Verstappen, but in fact it is a return to a challenging event he has contested before with Toyota - finishing 13th in 2020.

During his second stint at McLaren in the mid-2010s, Alonso became so disenchanted with the Honda-powered team’s competitiveness that he negotiated permission to contest the Indianapolis 500. He then took a sabbatical from F1 between 2018 and 2021, competing in the Indy 500 again as well as winning the Le Mans 24 Hours outright with Toyota in 2018 and 2019.

"Yes, exactly, I had to stop. I had to switch off from Formula 1," said Alonso of those experiences.

"I had to experience different formulas and different series, and learn from the specialists in those series and become a more complete driver. That was very important for me and I still find those challenges appealing. I don't know when I will do it, but I will repeat those experiences.

"I love challenges. My way of understanding motorsport and my way of living is around racing cars. It has been all my life and I think my strength has been to adapt to different cars, different rules: V10, V8, V6, Bridgestone, Michelin, Pirelli, KERS, hybrid, ground-effect cars, all these different things. Plus different series: prototypes, Indy, Dakar.

Alonso has already contested the Dakar, with Toyota in 2020 Photo by: Getty Images

"I try to use that strength and maybe do things that were possible in the 1960s, '80s or '90s and now probably no one will try. Max is the only one trying to do some GT racing. But apart from that, I like that challenge.

"I tried these things in the past and I will continue doing that. So maybe, yeah, you have more surprises in the next few weeks. There are things that people probably think that are impossible, but I want to find the limits of what is possible."

The Dakar Rally is an infamously challenging annual fixture which began life as the Paris-Dakar Rally, but was forced to shift location owing to instability in North Africa. After several years in South America it is now hosted by Saudi Arabia.

Alonso will drive an Aston-Martin branded car prepared by Prodrive, and based on the Dacia Sandrider which won the most recent running of the event in the hands of Nasser Al-Attiyah and co-driver Fabian Lurquin. Shortly after that, Dacia announced it would end its programme in the World Rally-Raid Championship (W2RC) a year earlier than originally planned, at the end of 2026 rather than the end of 2027.

The Sandrider itself was a development of a project which started life as the Prodrive Hunter, but was re-engined and rebodied to resemble the Dacia Manifesto concept car. The base vehicle lends itself to relatively straightforward re-engineering of body and powertrain.

Autosport understands that one of the plans on the table is to badge the new car as the Dreadnought, based on the virtual Aston Martin concept vehicle from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and style the body along the same lines.

Prodrive has a long history with Aston Martin. Founder David Richards served as chairman of the British marque from 2007 to 2013, and Prodrive ran Aston Martin’s successful GT and prototype sportscar racing programme.

The first tests with the Dacia Sandrider that will form the basis of the Dakar Aston Martin are reportedly due to take place within the next few weeks. Marc Coma, who partnered Alonso in 2020, is expected to return as his co-driver. The fellow Spaniard is a Dakar legend in his own right, having won the motorcycle category five times with KTM between 2006 and 2015.

The Dakar is unfinished business for Alonso, who finished 13th in 2020 Photo by: Getty Images

Prodrive is apparently planning to field a full Dakar team based around the Sandrider project rather than just a single car for Alonso and Coma. According to the Spanish reports, Al-Attiyah and Sebastien Loeb are also being considered as drivers. There has, however, been no official confirmation of the programme so far.

There is also uncertainty over where the 2027 Dakar Rally will actually take place. Until 2007, during its classic era, the event ran for decades from Europe into West Africa, usually finishing in Dakar. The 2008 edition had to be cancelled because of security concerns in Mauritania. From 2009 to 2019, the event retained the Dakar name but was held in South America, before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2020.

Officially, the 2027 Dakar is still scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia from 1-15 January. Organiser ASO has already published a detailed route comprising 13 stages and a total of 5,320 kilometres of competitive running. The FIA also continues to list Saudi Arabia as the official host country.

However, there is currently considerable uncertainty because of the geopolitical security situation in the Middle East. According to recent reports, ASO is therefore working on a contingency plan in which would Morocco step in as an alternative host.

A significantly more compact event of around eight stages is reportedly under consideration, although no final decision to move the rally to Morocco has been made.

Sports.title: Mercedes confirms Russell's Singapore GP grid penalty following Sepang retirement
Sports.content:
Mercedes has now confirmed that George Russell will take a grid penalty at this weekend’s Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix following his retirement in Malaysia.

The Mercedes driver was running third under the safety car, but then suddenly pulled over at Turn 1 with five laps remaining due to a power unit failure at Sepang last weekend.

It was subsequently presumed that his Silver Arrow would need a new engine for Singapore and if so, a grid penalty would be the consequence as Russell has already used the permitted four in a season.

So as published by Autosport on Tuesday and now confirmed by the Silver Arrows, Russell will start towards the back at Marina Bay this Sunday - a track he won at last year.

Team boss Toto Wolff said in Mercedes’ Singapore preview: “George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty, which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia.

“That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for.

“Unfortunately, these things are part of the sport and our focus now is on giving him the best possible car and opportunities to fight back through the field.

“We need to maximise this final sprint weekend of the year, keep learning, and score the strongest result we can with both cars. Singapore will be an important test of our understanding and our resilience as a team.”

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes, race start Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

This is particularly damning for Russell as he tries to claw back an 84-point deficit to his championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli with just seven rounds remaining.

It also means that he is now likely to miss out on the updated Mercedes engine under the Additional Development and Upgrades Opportunities system, which the team was planning to give him later in the season.

So Mercedes hopes now lay with Antonelli to get the team back to winning ways, after Red Bull’s Max Verstappen dominated from pole at Sepang with the Italian in second.

“Malaysia was obviously a very difficult weekend for us,” added Wolff. “We have spent the days since then working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been.

“We have identified several areas we need to investigate further, but F1 doesn’t offer simple answers and we need more evidence before drawing firm conclusions.

“Singapore gives us an immediate opportunity to continue that work. The characteristics of the circuit are very different and that will help us build a clearer picture of where we are.

“That is why we will evaluate both the latest update package and our previous specification across the weekend to ensure we fully understand the direction we need to take.”

Sports.title: Russell to take grid penalty in Singapore due to Sepang retirement
Sports.content:
George Russell is set to receive a grid penalty for this weekend’s Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix as a consequence of his retirement in Sepang last weekend.

The Mercedes driver was running third under the safety car with five laps remaining until he stopped at the Turn 1 entry due to a sudden failure in his power unit.

It means he needs a new engine for Marina Bay and, because he’s already churned through four power units in the 2026 season, any additional changes will incur a 10-place grid penalty.

That is what will happen this weekend, The Athletic has reported, and with the Singapore street circuit being notoriously difficult to overtake on, starting towards the back will make it incredibly difficult for Russell.

That does not do his title hopes any good because he heads into the weekend 84 points behind his championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who in September had a similar penalty at Monza.

But the 20-year-old sensation overcame that in the most impressive ways, by winning his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid - overtaking Russell on his way to victory.

It shows that churning through power units has been an issue for Mercedes amid an otherwise dominant year, with the Silver Arrows suffering unreliability on several occasions.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

Antonelli, for example, suffered an engine failure late in the Barcelona race, while a power unit problem forced Russell to retire from the lead in Montreal - similarly to Sepang.

So this forthcoming grid drop of his was long expected, but it is understood that Mercedes was hoping to do it later in the year - most likely Austin, the race after Singapore.

That’s because it has been granted one upgrade token under the new-for-2026 Additional Upgrades and Opportunities System (ADUO), which it is soon expected to fit.

Russell and Mercedes were therefore hoping to take the penalty on the weekend the ADUO engine gets fitted, but because that is no longer on the cards, he may miss out altogether.

This is something deputy team principal Bradley Lord confirmed could be the case following the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

“He came on the radio behind the safety car and said 'PU's starting to sound funny',” said Lord.

“We saw sensors then misbehaving and it was clear we had to pull the car over and we'd had a failure of some sort.

“Still need to understand what it means for his pool because he's not rich in low-mileage power units either. So that may mean we need to alter what had been our previous plan.”

Sports.title: What caused Mercedes' pace deficit at Sepang despite upgraded W17?
Sports.content:
Mercedes' performance at Formula 1's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will require further investigation as the conditions around the Sepang circuit made it difficult for the team to get a read on its latest update package.

The team introduced a revised floor and sidepod package for F1's first visit to Sepang in nine years, but it became apparent that the team was struggling to unlock its usual top-line pace throughout the weekend. Regardless, it was set to pick up a double podium finish before George Russell retired with a powertrain issue late on.

Through the weekend, the team declared itself happy with the performance of the update in higher-speed corners, but the W17 overall did not gel with the circuit - particularly around the slower corners.

In the team's usual post-race debrief circulated on its social media channels, deputy team principal Bradley Lord explained that the drivers were having to resort to slightly unusual inputs in those slower corners to get the car to bite.

"The combination potentially of update, track temperature and track surface caused an interaction and a set of behaviours that meant the car was not in its usual happy state, that the drivers were having to turn the car on the throttle in the slow corners," said Lord.

"That was further exacerbating the challenges with tyre temperature. So that's not an easy thing to unpick.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It's a bit of a 3D problem that we need to work through and then figure out exactly what steps we take going forward to make sure we've got the base understanding that we need to understand that the update is working well and that we're heading in the right direction in our development, not just for this year's car but for next year as well.

"So that's work that's going on at the moment back in the factory and also over in Singapore in order to establish exactly what the plan is for the coming days and the race weekend in Singapore."

Why Sepang's surface was a problem for more than just tyres

There are two particular threads that link the track surface to the car, the most obvious being the interaction between the road and the tyres. The roughness of the circuit was a key factor in excess tyre heat, as the contact between the tyre and the surface produced greater levels of strain on the tyre.

When the tyre makes contact with the road, it deforms elastically - meaning that the tyre would return to its natural state if the load was removed. This is exacerbated by the track surface; if, like Sepang, there are lots of gaps in the surface, the tyre will partly fill some of those gaps.

Although this produces grip through the mechanical movement of the tyre, the loading and unloading (known as hysteresis) of the contact patch will produce more heat as waste energy. Since the tyre deforms more to fill those pockets in the road surface, the heat generation on the tyre surface increases.

The second mechanism at play, which is of an aerodynamic nature, was one hinted at by McLaren team principal Andrea Stella. F1 cars not only use aero parts to generate load, but also to create certain flow patterns and even accelerate airflow to ensure the rest of the car works efficiently.

On a race track, the roughness of the track surface needs to be considered, as the airflow underneath the car can be affected by this. No circuit is completely smooth, and teams will likely have some idea of roughness to apply to their simulations.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

In a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation, the "domain" walls at the bottom will have a frictional coefficient applied to ensure the flow field is accurate. Wind tunnels may also use textured belts to produce a similar effect.

When you have such a unique track surface, however, it will cause a different interaction with the airflow under the car. If you imagine that this airflow under the car is being accelerated to help produce downforce, one can also assume that the surface texture will manipulate how this flow operates. The boundary layer – the theoretical immediate layer of a fluid around a surface – will change and may lead to effects like turbulence through separation.

Teams have much more data on Singapore, and thus the car's relative performance – from both a tyre and aerodynamic standpoint – should be much more easy to read. Lord also touched on Russell's power unit failure in Malaysia, noting that the Mercedes powerplant had suffered a mechanical failure but still required an investigation to determine the cause.

"Our investigation so far, we've got the car back, we've been able to do a first inspection. It's clearly a mechanical failure on the PU side," he said.

"Exactly what the root cause is, we still need to determine, but the consequence was clear for all to see. A devastating blow for the team and 15 points lost, but most especially, of course, for George, who was on for a very, very solid podium finish."

Sports.title: The dire consequence of Russell's Bahrain GP in Malaysia retirement
Sports.content:
George Russell’s retirement from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia will have huge consequences on the rest of his 2026 Formula 1 campaign - especially in regards to ADUO.

The Mercedes driver was running third under the safety car with five laps remaining at Sepang on Sunday, until he pulled over at the Turn 1 entry with a power unit failure.

Minds immediately went to what impact it would have on the title race, as second for team-mate Kimi Antonelli stretched his championship lead to 84 points with seven rounds left.

But Mercedes is also now having to reassess its plan of when to give Russell a new engine, considering it will incur a grid penalty as he’s already used the allotted four in a season.

“He came on the radio behind the safety car and said PU's starting to sound funny,” said Mercedes’ deputy team principal Bradley Lord.

“We saw sensors then misbehaving and it was clear we had to pull the car over and we'd had a failure of some sort.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Srinivasa Krishnan

“Still need to understand what it means for his pool because he's not rich in low mileage power units either. So that may mean we need to alter what had been our previous plan.”

The plan was for Russell’s next power unit to be the updated version under the Additional Development and Upgrades Opportunities system, which grants Mercedes one token.

It’s believed that the 28-year-old was set to take his penalty in Austin, but Sepang means he might need to do it beforehand - Singapore this weekend - and consequently miss out on the upgrade.

When asked if that’s the case, Lord confirmed: “Potentially so, yeah. That's what we need to understand. But yes, there may be a double whammy effect there, which for him after such a gut-wrenching blow today... it was devastating to see him have to pull off as he did.

"Yeah, there may be a sort of double whammy effect there that is just a really unfortunate consequence of that issue.”

Sepang continued what’s been a series of bad luck for the pre-season title favourite, who retired from the lead in Montreal with a power unit failure, as well as other misfortunes in 2026.

Bradley Lord, Mercedes Deputy Team Principal Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

But there’s also been issues on Antonelli’s side, such as his power unit failure late on at Barcelona, so unreliability is the one concern amid an otherwise dominant year for Mercedes.

“I’m so massively annoyed, I’m not in a happy place,” team boss Toto Wolff told Sky Sports after the Malaysian race.

“First of all, we didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will.

“Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us.

“We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

“So, as much as I love to be here when I look at the pure races, one of my worst experiences, to be honest.”

Mercedes is still on course for its first constructors’ title since 2021 as it leads second-placed Ferrari by 151 points, a gap that stood at 160 heading into Malaysia.

“This overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races,” added Wolff. “A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Sports.title: Russell admits his performance hasn’t been good enough this year regardless of luck | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell isn’t ruing his misfortune after his latest retirement in Sepang last weekend.

The Mercedes driver will take a grid drop penalty this weekend as Mercedes will fit a new power unit to his car. Russell has fallen 84 points behind his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli at the top of the championship standings.

But he feels his performance this year is a significant part of the reason why his championship hopes have faded.

“I don’t feel my performance has been good enough this year, independent of good luck and bad luck,” said Russell. “I feel that whenever I do have bad luck, of course I can be disappointed about it, but I want to focus on the things I can control first.”

Russell beat Antonelli 21-3 in qualifying sessions for grands prix last season. But Antonelli has held the upper hand this year and leads Russell 9-7 ahead of this weekend’s race (see graph below).

“All of my years in Formula 1, I’ve always had a great record against my team mates,” said Russell. “Especially in qualifying I think it was sort of like 80-20 in my qualifying records. This year I’m, I don’t know, 40-60 or maybe even less.

“So that really shows I haven’t done a good enough job this season, independent of the good luck or the bad luck. So I guess that’s why it maybe isn’t affecting me as much. As it would in different circumstances. And, you know, every weekend I just wake up, look at myself in the mirror and think what I can do better.”

Russell expects he will have to take another engine penalty before the year is over.

“Obviously, if you could choose where to take the penalty in the season, this would be probably the second-bottom of the list after Monaco,” he said. “But unfortunately, just with how things have panned out, we have no choice but to take it here.

Sports.title: Norris says fuel system problem has “cost me quite a lot” in recent races | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris is “hopeful” McLaren have solved a problem with his car’s fuel system which he claims has compromised his performance in recent rounds.

The McLaren driver says he has been losing speed on straights compared to his team mate because of the problem. McLaren believe they have identified the cause.

However Norris pointed out the potential gain from the fix won’t be as significant in Singapore due to the Marina Bay circuit’s lack of long straights.

“I need to get on track first and see how much better it is,” he said. “It’s obviously also a circuit where straights are not the highest priority and [it won’t be] as detrimental as the last few weekends.

“But nevertheless, you always want to go down the straights as quick as you should be able to. It’s always tough when you come out of corners better and end up going slower.”

Norris won in Hungary and the Netherlands and came close to victory in Madrid. He took pole position at all three rounds, but only managed fifth on the grid in the previous two races, which he believes was partly due to the problem on his car.

“It’s been a frustrating two weekends trying to figure out what the issue’s been and why there’s just been a constant lack of straight-line speed and performance,” he said. “Especially in this kind of battle we’ve been in, the last two qualifying [sessions] it’s been two or three positions. So it’s cost me quite a lot.

“At the same time, there’s obviously things I can do better as well. But I’m confident that the team have done a good job. They put a lot of work into trying to figure out things and I’m hopeful that it’ll be better this weekend. But I have to get out on track and see first.”

Sports.title: “I deserve to be in Formula 1”: Ocon rules out racing elsewhere in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon is not interested in racing in another series next year if he cannot find a Formula 1 drive.

Haas announced last week Ocon will not return to drive for them next year. Although there are few places remaining on the grid for 2027, Ocon is committed to remaining in F1.

“That’s where I deserve to be,” he said. “If I look at the results and what I’ve shown in Formula 1, I deserve to be in Formula 1.

“Of course, there are other categories which are fantastic as well. But I want to be racing in Formula 1, in the next five, seven years. That’s what I want to be.

“So I will keep pushing to be that position. In the near future, that’s the only thing I’m looking at so far.”

Ocon made his F1 debut in 2016. He has raced every year since there except in 2019, when he lost his seat at Racing Point to Lance Stroll, and spent a season as a test driver for Mercedes. He said he would consider a similar arrangement if he cannot find a race seat for next year.

“If there are no possibilities to race next year, that’s what I will do,” he said.

“I’m still working on it, still discussing,” he added. “When I have more news I will announce something definitely, but at the moment, full focus is on this weekend.”

Sports.title: Antonelli was so quick in Formula 4 Mercedes swapped his engine to check | Other motorsport
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s speed in Formula 4 surprised Mercedes so much they decided to check he didn’t have an engine advantage.

Williams team principal James Vowles, who worked on Mercedes’ young driver during his time at the team, explained why Antonelli’s performance impressed them. He started his first full season in the Italian Formula 4 championship in 2022.

“He was fantastic in karting, but you’re never quite sure how karting will translate into single-seater,” Vowles told the official Formula 1 channel. “But it was the first year of single seater where he didn’t just win, there was a gap of two-and-a-half tenths between him and anyone else.

“That doesn’t happen in Formula 4. Everyone put it down to ‘he’s done lots of testing’ [but] he didn’t: he did six days of testing.”

Vowles said he, along with Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff and young driver programme head Gwen Lagrue, decided to check Antonelli’s lead over his rivals was down to him and not his car.

“What we also had a question – and this was between Toto, myself and Gwen, we were having this conversation – do we have just a bias [because] we’ve got a good chassis and good engine?

“So at one point in the season, we took the engine out and put another engine in. We purposely swapped it around and still went on to win.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“So at that point, if you’d asked me, I would have said that he’s very, very good. I’ve rarely seen that transition into it. And he continued that on through his junior career.”

Antonelli won 13 out of 22 races in F4 that year, then won the Formula Regional European Championship the following season. At that point Mercedes decided to accelerate his progression to F1.

“Mercedes did a very brave call, and the right call, which was to move him up all the way into F2 straight away and then to a very aggressive [F1] programme in the background,” said Vowles. “And I think without doubt, he probably suffered from the fact that it was a very fast acceleration into F1. So he had a year of playing catch-up.”

Following a difficult first season in F1, Antonelli has thrived this year and holds an 84-point lead over team mate George Russell at the top of the championship standings with seven rounds remaining.

Vowles admitted he was surprised by the progress Antonelli has made between his first two seasons in F1. “Well done to Toto and the team, [it was a] brave call. Absolutely came out trumps on top of it. Great belief.

“Because at times, if you read some of the headlines, everyone was questioning what they were doing. I knew underneath that he had a huge performance.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The step he’s made this year I think probably caught most people out. Maybe not the team, maybe they had more awareness of this, but for me I’m very impressed with the jump he’s made.

“Because it’s not just the pace that comes with it, there’s no mistakes that go with it either. Particularly [because] he’s in control of the situation.

“He carved his way from the back of the grid to the front at Monza. That’s a mature drive. It’s a hard drive to do. I think I looked at it on that one. I thought, how the hell’s he made eight positions up? Anyway, good on him.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: No F1 track changes in Monaco? That’s a good thing | Briefs
Sports.content:
The Monaco Grand Prix promoter has rejected calls for more changes to the 97-year-old Formula 1 venue following complaints drivers find it too difficult to pass.

Reader @Roger-Ayles is pleased the Monte-Carlo circuit will stay the way it is:

I’m fine with that because I love Monaco for what it is, A somewhat unique challenge that is closer than almost everywhere else to what the sport used to be. Circuits that were a challenge, Where mistakes are costly and where a driver needs to maintain concentration for 90-plus minutes knowing that a small mistake and tap of the barrier could end there day. In an era of mile-wide circuits with miles of runoff and ‘street’ circuits that are also really wide with a lot more room for error than street circuits used to provide the fact we have retained one historic true street circuit that still features most of the elements that used to make such circuits so unique & challenging is welcome as far as I’m concerned. As people keep saying to fans like me who dislike the sprints and so on: If you don’t like this race then just don’t watch it, but I for one shall continue to watch and enjoy the Monaco Grand Prix! Although been a sprint next year and given how I really dislike the sprint format I shall sadly from my point of view not be watching any of the Friday or Saturday track action for next years race.
