Sports.title: FIA to introduce further F1 software update after farcical start to Sepang race | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The FIA will introduce further changes to its engine software following the farcical scenes at last weekend’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The motorsport governing body also disputed claims its software was not adequately tested before the stoppages which struck multiple cars in Sepang.

Several Red Bull-Ford, Ferrari and Audi-powered cars slowed drastically during the formation lap before the start of Sunday’s race. Race control abandoned its attempt to start the race and the FIA made changes to its software in order for the start to proceed.

The FIA confirmed the fault occured due to its software which restricts how much power a driver may use at different points around the lap. The requirement is a feature of the new power unit regulations introduced for 2026.

“Some cars running on low engine RPM in certain circuit sectors where a 250kW power reduction was applied experienced a loss of power beyond the original intent and that could not be recovered in those sectors,” it said.

No further changes are planned for this weekend’s round in Singapore. Teams have only a single, hour-long practice session this weekend as it is a sprint event. The FIA intends to make further revisions to its software ahead of the following round in Austin.

“The configuration established for the Sepang event will be reinstated for the Singapore Grand Prix should similar weather conditions be expected. Additionally, a further update to the wet weather software will be released for the United States Grand Prix on October 25.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The governing body denied claims the software was not adequately tested prior to last weekend’s race, which was the 16th round of the season.

“The FIA would like to address comments suggesting that the software had not been tested prior to its deployment. Before implementation, teams and Power Unit manufacturers conducted simulation exercises to validate the software package, which was subsequently tested in full-scale running during Free Practice 1 sessions at both the Belgian Grand Prix and the Dutch Grand Prix.”

FIA statement on Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia start failures

FIA concludes investigation into Bahrain GP in Malaysia formation lap “software bug” The FIA has completed a thorough review of the circumstances which necessitated the release of a Power Unit software configurations upgrade ahead of the race start of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The review focused on these key areas: The precise cause of the loss of power experienced by a number of cars on the formation lap

Measures that can be introduced to mitigate a recurrence of the same issues

The future management of wet-weather Power Unit settings (energy limit restraints)

Learnings from the data from individual team and Power Unit manufacturers

The review concluded that some cars running on low engine RPM in certain circuit sectors where a 250kW power reduction was applied experienced a loss of power beyond the original intent and that could not be recovered in those sectors. As a result, the configuration established for the Sepang event will be reinstated for the Singapore Grand Prix should similar weather conditions be expected. Additionally, a further update to the wet weather software will be released for the United States Grand Prix on October 25.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

The review also recommended that measures would be implemented for testing of the software, recognising that opportunities for testing are limited, to make it robust as possible. The FIA , together with the teams and Power Unit Manufacturers (PUMs), will continue to strengthen Power Unit software testing and verification capabilities, enhancing the overall validation process through independent assessment and collaborative feedback, including input from the supplier of the standardised Electronics Control Unit (ECU). The FIA would like to address comments suggesting that the software had not been tested prior to its deployment. Before implementation, teams and Power Unit manufacturers conducted simulation exercises to validate the software package, which was subsequently tested in full-scale running during Free Practice 1 sessions at both the Belgian Grand Prix and the Dutch Grand Prix. On Sunday, the sequence of software installation and integration was as follows: 15:45: The race start procedure was suspended following two formation laps after a number of cars experienced power loss issues. 15:50: Within five minutes of the suspension the FIA technical team had identified the cause of the issue and released an updated Power Unit software configurations designed to address the problem. 16:03: Eighteen minutes after the suspension the FIA provided teams with further technical guidance and clarifications in response to implementation, installation and operation of the revised software configurations.

Sports.title: Spotlight: Formula E’s chief executive says he can’t sit through a Formula 1 race | Briefs
Sports.content:
The claim that young people lack the attention span to follow long-format material was one of Formula 1’s justifications for introducing shorter sprint races as an alternative to grands prix in 2021.

Now Formula E’s chief executive Jeff Dodds has made a similar claim, but only offered one point to support his belief: his own inability to sit through a grand prix.

“I think the next generation of motorsport fans doesn’t have the attention span to watch for 90 minutes,” he said in a recent interview.

“I won’t stick around and watch the whole race. I watch the start of it, I go missing for the middle of it and I come back and watch at the end.”

Sports.title: Monaco rules out making changes to its Formula 1 track layout | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The president of the Automobile Club de Monaco says it will not make changes to the layout of the famous circuit.

The 3.3 kilometre circuit is the shortest and narrowest on the calendar. It has frequently been criticised for producing processional races because Formula 1 cars find it so difficult to overtake.

Although the track’s configuration has been revised many times since its first grand prix in 1929, the limited space available in the Principality makes significant alterations and widening impossible. Monaco has reclaimed land from the sea for construction purposes, such as when the ‘Nouvelle’ chicane was built 40 years ago, but ACM president Michel Boeri denied they plan to do so in future.

“Very importantly, the circuit will not be changed, contrary to what I’ve heard many people suggest,” he told Nice-Matin. “Demolishing this or moving that would automatically trigger a fresh review of the circuit and require new FIA homologation.”

Formula 1 has extended its contract to race in Monaco twice in the last two years. Its current deal will keep it on the calendar until at least 2035.

Boeri said F1 promoters Liberty Media saw the value of keeping one of the most historic venues on the calendar.

“They’re not here out of charity,” he said. “They’re here to make money. And we’re here to give them as little as possible and make as much as possible ourselves. It’s a straightforward, fair contest in an open market.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Our American friends realised how responsive we could be. Unlike those who still call Monaco ‘the merry-go-round’ and would do well to update their thinking, we reached an understanding in principle that the grand prix is a major draw for Formula 1. We weren’t going to be constantly hassled over whether a kerb had two or three too many corners.”

However Boeri indicated Monaco may find a way to increase the space available in the pit lane. “The grand prix’s future is secured until 2035, but with this platform and the building that will be constructed on it, we might be able to rethink the grid area and perhaps even extend the contract further,” he said, “All of that remains to be defined.

“It’s no secret, for example, that the pit lane will be difficult to sustain much longer. Space is limited, and the garages aren’t wide enough. And when you don’t have width on the ground, you build upward.

“I can already hear all the non possumus [‘not possible’] objections that will come from this area, but eventually people will see reason. I’m no gardener, but there’s more than one kind of tree, for example.”

The difficulty of overtaking in Monaco led F1 to introduce a rules change last year forcing drivers to make two tyre changes. The result was an even more processional race in which several cars deliberately lapped very slowly, prompting criticism from drivers which led to the rule being dropped.

Monaco will hold a sprint race for the first time next year, a decision which surprised many due to the difficulty of overtaking at the track.

Sports.title: Bektemir Melikuziev Calls for WBA to Strip Munguia Over Mandatory Snub
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev accused Jaime Munguia of refusing their ordered WBA super middleweight title fight, writing on Instagram Thursday morning that he had accepted concessions on preparation, drug testing, and pay to secure his mandatory shot.

His complaint came before news of Munguia’s proposed October 31 fight against Nikita Zon on the Canelo Alvarez–Christian Mbilli card in Riyadh. Melikuziev’s account raises a question for the champion’s team: what is preventing the mandatory defense if the challenger has accepted everything asked of him?

“I agreed to fight Jaime Munguia on short notice, without a proper training camp. I agreed to fight without VADA testing, even though we have always insisted on it. I even agreed to accept the lowest possible purse or no purse at all,” Melikuziev wrote on Instagram. “We made every concession possible to make this fight happen. And yet, my team has now informed me that Munguia is still refusing to fight me.”

Those are Melikuziev’s claims about the negotiations. His willingness to accept those terms does not establish that an agreement was completed, but it puts pressure on Munguia’s team to explain why another opponent is being pursued.

“So I have one simple question: Why hasn’t a purse bid been ordered? And if the champion refuses to fulfill his mandatory obligation, why hasn’t he been stripped of his title?” Melikuziev wrote.

The WBA gave the teams until October 21 to negotiate, so that deadline has not yet expired. However, Melikuziev is asking the organization to act if Munguia is refusing the ordered defense while pursuing another opponent.

“Stop acting as if there is no mandatory and no rules,” Melikuziev wrote.

Later Thursday, the WBA announced that it had not approved Munguia–Zon and reaffirmed Melikuziev’s status as the official challenger.

Melikuziev further alleged that Munguia wanted more money to face him and offered to stage the fight in Uzbekistan with additional funding. That financial account remains his version of events.

For Munguia, scheduling Zon does not resolve the mandatory. Melikuziev says he has removed every obstacle on his side. Munguia’s team now faces the question of what remains on theirs.

Sports.title: WBA Has Not Approved Jaime Munguia–Nikita Zon Fight
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia’s proposed October 31 fight against Nikita Zon has not received WBA approval, the sanctioning body announced Thursday night, reminding his team that Bektemir Melikuziev remains the mandatory challenger for his super middleweight title.

The statement puts an obstacle in front of the planned Riyadh appearance. Munguia has been named to face Zon, but the WBA has already ordered him to negotiate a defense against Melikuziev.

“The WBA has not approved the Jaime Munguia vs. Nikita Zon bout. Bektemir Melikuziev is the official contender in the super middleweight division,” the organization posted on its official X account on October 8. “The WBA will review the situation.”

That leaves Munguia’s team needing a ruling before it can present the Zon matchup as an approved WBA title defense. The announcement of an opponent has not settled the championship obligation.

The WBA ordered Munguia–Melikuziev on September 21, giving the teams until October 21 to reach an agreement. Its published order stated that Munguia’s 120-day mandatory defense period expired on August 30. If negotiations fail, or either side refuses to negotiate, the championship committee may call a purse bid.

That deadline falls just ten days before the proposed Zon fight. Unless the WBA grants an exception or approves another arrangement, the mandatory order remains an obstacle to Munguia defending his belt against someone else.

Munguia could risk losing his WBA title if he goes ahead with Zon without approval. The organization has already ordered him to negotiate with Melikuziev, and announcing another opponent does not suspend that obligation or stop the October 21 deadline.

Melikuziev should not have to wait indefinitely while Munguia pursues a different fight. He is the mandatory challenger, negotiations have been ordered, and the WBA has publicly confirmed that the proposed Zon defense has not been approved.

The WBA has not announced a stripping decision. However, if Munguia proceeds without an exception, he risks entering the Zon fight with his championship on the line outside the ring.

Sports.title: Iglesias Drops Oliver Zaren Twice, Scores 7th round stoppage
Sports.content:
IBF and IBO super middleweight champion Osleys “El Tornado” Iglesias broke down Oliver “The Great Dane” Zaren, scoring two sixth-round knockdowns before stopping the Danish challenger in the seventh on Thursday at Capitole de Quebec in Quebec City, Canada.

The Cuban southpaw’s first IBF title defense headlined Camille Estephan’s Eye of the Tiger card, streamed on DAZN. Iglesias gradually wore down his larger opponent before turning a one-sided contest into a decisive finish.

Zaren’s size and toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not land enough punches to slow the champion’s attack. Iglesias continued finding him with clean shots, increasing the punishment as the rounds passed.

The sixth was particularly damaging for Zaren. Iglesias put him down twice and left him with a cut over his left eyebrow. The challenger continued into the seventh, but his trainer, former super middleweight champion Mikkel Kessler, threw in the towel to prevent further punishment. The stoppage came at 1:31, with Eddie Claudio refereeing the scheduled 12-round contest.

Iglesias, who is based in Berlin, followed his title-winning victory over Pavel Silyagin with another stoppage. Zaren, from Roskilde, Denmark, showed determination in his first world title challenge, but the fight exposed how much more he needed offensively to compete with the champion.

Wilkens Mathieu Takes Split Decision Over Vladimir Shishkin

In the co-feature, Montreal’s Wilkens Mathieu retained his NABF super middleweight title with a split-decision victory over Vladimir Shishkin in a 10-round contest.

Two judges scored the fight 98-92 for Mathieu, while the third favored Shishkin 97-93. The divided scoring reflected a fight in which Shishkin’s boxing skills gave Mathieu considerably more to deal with than Iglesias faced in the main event.

Mathieu looked for heavy punches but did not always follow them with enough regular work, allowing Shishkin to compete through his more measured boxing. Steve St-Germain was the referee.

Dzmitry Asanau Outpoints Luis Santana

Dzmitry “The Wasp” Asanau defeated Montreal’s Luis Santana by unanimous decision over 10 rounds at lightweight, adding Santana’s NABF title to his IBF Intercontinental and WBC Continental Americas belts.

Asanau dropped Santana with a left jab to the chin in the third round. The judges scored the bout 98-91 twice and 97-92. Junior Padulo Jr. refereed.

Imam Khataev Knocks Out Padraig McCrory

NABF light heavyweight champion Imam Khataev needed just 69 seconds to knock out Belfast’s Padraig “The Hammer” McCrory in their scheduled 10-round bout.

Khataev landed a left hook to the head that dropped McCrory, who could not beat the count. Junior Padulo Jr. was the referee.

Leila Beaudoin Wins Every Round On The Cards

Leila Beaudoin, of Lévis, Quebec, defeated Argentina’s Brisa “La China” Alfonzo by unanimous decision in their 10-round super featherweight contest.

Beaudoin dropped Alfonzo with a body shot in the sixth round, with the challenger taking an eight-count before continuing. All three judges scored the fight 100-89. Alain Villeneuve refereed.

Daylen Pepin Stops Matias Pinilla

Quebec’s Daylen Pepin stopped Chile’s Matias Pinilla at 2:59 of the fourth round in their lightweight contest.

A flurry from Pepin brought the finish in the round’s final seconds. Jeff Topping was the referee.

Jacob Blais Defeats Yoan Trottier

Montreal welterweight Jacob Blais earned a unanimous decision over Quebec City’s Yoan Trottier in a four-round bout.

Trottier suffered a cut over his right eyebrow in the second round. All three judges scored the contest 40-36 for Blais, with Jeff Topping refereeing.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Batters Oliver Zaren Into Seventh-Round Stoppage
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias slowly battered his larger challenger Oliver Zaren into a seventh-round stoppage on Thursday night, retaining his IBF and IBO super middleweight titles at Théâtre Capitole in Quebec City.

Zaren’s trainer, former champion Mikkel Kessler, threw in the towel in the seventh after watching his fighter absorb sustained punishment. The Dane’s toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not produce enough offense to change its direction.

Iglesias (16-0, 15 KOs) had to work longer than he has against some of his previous opponents, steadily breaking Zaren down rather than ending the contest with an early knockout. The challenger took the shots and continued trying, giving the Cuban time to demonstrate how effectively he can wear down an opponent who doesn’t go away immediately.

“I hope the winner [Canelo-Mbilli] faces me. I’d like my next fight to be a Unification,” said Iglesias about wanting to fight the winner of the October 31st fight between WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli and Canelo Alvarez.

Zaren looked bigger, but that size did little to slow Iglesias. The champion controlled the contest and landed cleanly, increasing his output as the rounds passed. Zaren was spending too much of the fight absorbing punches without delivering enough back to make Iglesias hesitate.

That was the difference between surviving and competing. Zaren remained on his feet, but there was little reason to expect the fight to turn in his favor. Kessler eventually made the decision his fighter’s durability had delayed, preventing further punishment in a contest that had become one-sided.

The 26-year-old Zaren (19-1-1, 8 KOs) entered his first world title challenge ranked fifth by the IBF. His unbeaten record had been built without a victory over a leading super middleweight, and Iglesias exposed how much more was required at championship level.

For Iglesias, 28, this was his first IBF defense after winning the vacant belt against Pavel Silyagin in April. He has now stopped Vladimir Shishkin, Silyagin and Zaren in consecutive fights.

Bigger names remain the next test. Zaren gave Iglesias rounds and showed considerable toughness, but he never forced the champion to fight on his terms. Iglesias leaves Quebec with another challenger worn down and another stoppage on his record.

Sports.title: Wilkens Mathieu Takes Split Verdict Over Vladimir Shishkin
Sports.content:
Wilkens Mathieu retained his NABF super middleweight title with a disputed split-decision win over Vladimir Shishkin on Thursday night, with many viewers believing the veteran’s boxing skills deserved the verdict at the Capitole de Québec.

Two judges scored the ten-round fight 98-92 for Mathieu, while the third favored Shishkin 97-93. The bout was the co-feature on the Eye of the Tiger card headlined by Osleys Iglesias against Oliver Zaren, streamed on DAZN.

Mathieu, 21, spent too much of the fight loading up on punches rather than letting his hands go with quicker shots. He looked for power when a steadier flow of punches and combinations could have helped him build his offense.

That approach gave Shishkin time to read his attacks and use his experience. The 35-year-old former world-title challenger applied pressure and made Mathieu work, producing stretches where his power punches quieted the hometown crowd.

Shishkin’s skills were a major part of the difficulty. Mathieu had the younger legs, but the veteran showed that youth and punching power do not automatically overcome an opponent who knows how to interrupt an attack and make his own work count.

Mathieu had his successes and finished strongly in the tenth. However, many fans felt Shishkin had already done enough to win. The disagreement was about who deserved the decision, rather than simply whether Mathieu had faced a tougher fight than expected.

The two 98-92 totals were especially striking. Both judges gave Mathieu eight rounds, a wide margin for a fight in which Shishkin repeatedly troubled him. The third judge’s 97-93 score for Shishkin reflected a very different reading of the action.

Mathieu entered following an eighth-round stoppage of Olympic silver medalist Esquiva Falcao in June at the same venue. Shishkin brought experience from his IBF title defeat against William Scull and his stoppage loss to Iglesias.

The result keeps Mathieu moving toward bigger fights at 168 pounds, but his performance leaves questions about that pace. Against better opposition, loading up without enough punches between the power shots could cost him rounds that he cannot recover with a strong finish.

Sports.title: Imam Khataev Demolishes Padraig McCrory In One Round
Sports.content:
Imam Khataev demolished Padraig McCrory in the first round Thursday night, retaining his NABF light heavyweight title with a knockout at 1:09 at the Théâtre Capitole in Quebec City.

The Olympic bronze medalist needed little more than a minute to end the scheduled 10-round contest on the DAZN-streamed Eye of the Tiger card headlined by Osleys Iglesias against Oliver Zaren. Khataev improves to 13-1 with 12 knockouts, while McCrory drops to 20-3 with 10 KOs.

A left hand to the side of McCrory’s head put the Belfast fighter down, leaving him unable to beat the count. The broadcast commentary described the punch as affecting his equilibrium. Although McCrory’s reaction briefly suggested a body shot, the damage was attributed to the head punch.

There was no opportunity for McCrory to work his way back into the fight. Khataev’s power settled it before the challenger could establish anything, turning what was supposed to be a full night’s work into another short appearance.

The result gives Khataev his third consecutive victory since losing a split decision to David Morrell in July 2025. He had already stopped Adam Deines and Mickael Diallo during that rebuilding run.

McCrory was a substantial underdog, and the speed of the finish showed how little room he had for error against a puncher like Khataev. Coming out of a brief retirement after a June farewell victory, he found himself facing an opponent whose power was far beyond what that comeback win had prepared him for.

Khataev handled the opponent in front of him, but this was too brief to reveal much about his development since the Morrell defeat. His punching power was already established. The next useful test would be someone who can survive those early exchanges and force him to make adjustments over several rounds.

That is the challenge for his handlers now. Another quick knockout keeps Khataev moving, but tougher opposition would give a clearer picture of how close he is to another fight against a leading light heavyweight.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Targets Opetaia, Beterbiev, Usyk and Fury
Sports.content:
David Benavidez laid out a wish list featuring Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, Oleksandr Usyk and Tyson Fury, but his willingness to skip ahead to Usyk shows how quickly his cruiserweight plans could change.

“We got two great fights at cruiserweight before we get up there first,” Benavidez said to Inside Ring Show. “We got Jai Opetaia, then I think Beterbiev is going to come up to cruiserweight.” “If we can get a fight in with Usyk and Tyson Fury, then that’s something I’m willing to do.”

Benavidez appears to smell the money available at heavyweight. He describes his ambitions as a search for greatness, but Usyk and Fury also offer the possibility of enormous paydays. His interest extends beyond spending years building a cruiserweight reign.

The proposed sequence assumes plenty. Benavidez would need to secure those fights and win them to keep building toward the next one. Opetaia could derail that route through his southpaw combinations, movement, and experience at 200 pounds.

Beterbiev brings another threat, although Benavidez says there is interest from the other side.

“Beterbiev has definitely reached out to our team, and he’s been actively trying to make that fight,” he said.

That is more concrete than simply naming an opponent, but it still leaves the weight, timing, and agreement unresolved.

More revealing was Benavidez’s response to the possibility of Opetaia fighting Deontay Wilder. Rather than waiting, he suggested taking his business straight to heavyweight.

“If we can’t get that fight for Cinco de Mayo with Jai Opetaia, then we’ll do it with Usyk.”

That would be a substantial leap. Usyk’s movement and accuracy would test whether Benavidez could apply his pressure against an elite heavyweight. Fury’s size and reach would create a different set of difficulties.

Benavidez’s ambition is clear. What remains uncertain is how much of this list he can turn into reality. Naming four major opponents is easy compared with negotiating the fights and beating the men across from him.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol’s Vanishing Hunger Exposed
Sports.content:
Dmitry Bivol knows who he wants in the ring, but he is in no rush to lock down a contract. During an appearance on Inside the Ring, the champion singled out Artur Beterbiev, Canelo Alvarez, plus David Benavidez as his top targets. Still, he refused to pick one or name a date.

“This is Beterbiev, this is Canelo, and this is Benavidez,” Bivol said to Inside Ring Show. “This is three most big fights, I think, for me now.”

Bivol has the names ready. What is missing is any real urgency to get these bouts signed.

When asked about completing the Beterbiev trilogy by May, Bivol mentioned he would accept that timeline if all sides agreed. He pointed out that past talks hit roadblocks. That leaves fans with another vague target instead of a firm date. Waiting longer simply means Beterbiev gets older.

They split their previous two bouts. Unfinished business remains. Delaying the rubber match alters the physical test. While that does not prove Bivol wants to age his rival out, the advantage definitely leans his way.

Targeting Canelo makes pure financial sense. Bivol dominated their first clash, neutralizing the smaller boxer with ease. A return bout promises massive money against someone whose style he already mastered. Extra ring wear on Canelo only tilts the odds further in Bivol’s favor.

Benavidez offers a totally unique puzzle. Yet Bivol gave zero clues about when he wants that clash. He never clarified if he would jump to cruiserweight either.

Looking at other belts produced similar noncommittal answers. Bivol talked about how tough it feels jumping from 175 to 200 pounds, but skipped any mention of challenging Jai Opetaia.

His back surgery definitely plays a role in camp routines. He admits he must train smarter these days, which makes total sense. Even so, the core mystery lingers. Which major challenge does he actually want next?

Right now, Bivol is focusing entirely on Callum Smith. Past that date, his big plans stay strictly hypothetical. Something has changed with Bivol since his rematch with Beterbiev in February 2025. That twelfth round against Beterbiev took something out of him that a doctor cannot fix.

Bivol can talk all he wants about back rehabilitation and careful training camps, but the hesitation in his matchmaking tells the real story. When a fighter gets dragged into deep water, absorbs damage, and feels the fight slipping away beneath him with seconds left on the clock, it changes his wiring. Bivol survived that final barrage to collect the decision, but he walked away knowing exactly how violent that rivalry is. The appetite to jump straight back in with Beterbiev or any tough opponent has vanished.

Putting Canelo and Benavidez on a public wishlist is standard diversion. Canelo is a safe, massive payday against an opponent Bivol already solved without breaking a sweat. Benavidez is locked into cruiserweight campaigns, giving Bivol the perfect out to claim weight disparities prevent the bout. Meanwhile, Beterbiev is on the other side of forty, yet Bivol will not commit to a date to finish business.

Taking the Callum Smith fight while slow-walking the rubber match proves the point. Bivol went from an active technician hunting undisputed status to a cautious champion protecting his brand. When an elite boxer starts looking for reasons not to fight the very guys who tested his chin, the hunger is gone.

Ghana News.title: Nzema chiefs honour Lands Minister, demand sustainable revival of Adamus Resources
Ghana News.content:
The Paramount Chief of the Eastern Nzema Traditional Area, Awulae Blay IX, has led a delegation of chiefs and Queen Mothers to honour the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, while urging the government to ensure that the planned revival of Adamus Resources Limited delivers jobs, investment and lasting economic benefits to the Nzema area.

The delegation, comprising sub-chiefs and Queen Mothers, conferred a developmental chieftaincy title on Mr Buah in recognition of his contribution to Ellembelle and the wider Nzema area.

Awulae Blay IX also commended the Minister for his efforts to sustain the legacy of Ghana’s first President, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah, particularly through the annual Nkrumafest celebration. A traditional stool was presented to the Minister to symbolise the honour.

The chiefs used the courtesy call to urge the Ministry to closely monitor the government’s 12-month roadmap for Adamus Resources, stressing that the mine’s revival should translate into jobs, improved livelihoods and investment opportunities for local communities.

They also petitioned President John Dramani Mahama, through the Minister, to consider renaming Ghana Gas as “Atuabo Gas” to strengthen the sense of local ownership of the facility.

Responding, Mr Buah thanked the traditional authorities for the honour and reaffirmed his commitment to the development of Nzema and the Western Region.

He said the committee established by the President to oversee Adamus Resources had been tasked with ensuring that the company settles its outstanding liabilities, develops a sustainable revival plan and attracts fresh capital, including through potential equity participation by additional partners.

The Minister said Adamus Resources would engage the traditional authorities to hear their concerns and incorporate them into the revival process, with the ultimate aim of ensuring sustainable operations and tangible benefits for the people of Nzema.

He also assured the delegation that government would continue to address development needs in the area, including roads and other critical infrastructure.

Ghana News.title: ExxonMobil return talks emerge as GIPA CEO holds back details
Ghana News.content:
Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) CEO Simon Madjie says there have been talks about ExxonMobil returning to Ghana. But he declined to disclose details, leaving further comment to the energy authorities.

“I knew that there were some talks for them to come back. It's not something that can be disclosed now.”

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, Mr Madjie referred questions about the discussions to the Minister of Energy and the Petroleum Commission.

“So I, I think you leave that entirely to the Minister of Energy and Petroleum Commission.”

His remarks offered a limited indication of discussions about a possible return. He gave no timeline or terms. He also did not say how far the talks had progressed.

The issue arose when the host asked about multinational companies seeking to enter or return to Ghana’s petroleum sector. The host recalled earlier comments from the Energy Minister about companies such as Shell and ExxonMobil.

Mr Madjie initially outlined other developments in the sector. He said the Petroleum Commission and the ministry would have much of the detail.

“But what we all know is that from the Africa Oil Week, Chevron and Shell signed an MOU to look at work in the Eastern Keta Basin. So that's ongoing.”

He also cited reported interest from Petrobras in examining some of Ghana’s petroleum acreages and blocks.

Alongside that interest, Mr Madjie pointed to investment announcements by companies already operating in the country.

He cited plans by the Jubilee partners to invest $2 billion and drill 20 wells in the Jubilee field. He also referred to a $1.5 billion announcement by ENI and its partners.

“And so there's a lot of activities within that space. I'm sure folks at the Petroleum Commission will give you a lot more technical details.”

But when the host returned specifically to ExxonMobil, Mr Madjie held back. His response acknowledged talks about a return without confirming an agreement or a decision by the company to resume operations.

Ghana News.title: Council of State meets teacher unions over strike today
Ghana News.content:
The Council of State is set to engage teacher unions on Friday, October 9, as efforts intensify to resolve the industrial action by pre-tertiary teachers over outstanding employment-related concerns.

The meeting, scheduled for 1:00 p.m. at the Council’s Secretariat, will bring together representatives of the unions and Council members to discuss issues including delayed promotions, deprived-area allowances and negotiations on a Collective Bargaining Agreement with the Ministry of Education.

An invitation signed on behalf of the Chairman of the Council’s Economic and Social Development Committee, HRM Drolor Rosso Adamtey I, said the engagement would allow the unions to present their concerns to the Council.

The National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT) and the Pre-Tertiary Teachers Association of Ghana (PRETAG) have cited these outstanding matters among the reasons for their industrial action.

Meanwhile, Controller and Accountant-General Kwasi Agyei says his department has processed the promotion records of 52,000 teachers and received the required input forms from the Ghana Education Service (GES). He said the update was as of 2 p.m. on Thursday, October 8, paving the way for the necessary verification ahead of salary adjustments and payment of arrears.

The processing follows a September 28 directive by Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu asking the GES Director-General to submit the relevant data to facilitate payments. Friday’s meeting is expected to provide a platform for discussions on the remaining concerns as stakeholders seek a resolution to the dispute.

Ghana News.title: Ntim Fordjour appeals to Mahama to abandon regulation restricting preaching in buses
Ghana News.content:
Senior Pastor of Victory Bible Church International’s Higher Heights Sanctuary in East Legon and Assin South MP, Rev. John Ntim Fordjour, has appealed to President John Dramani Mahama to intervene over regulations restricting preaching in moving commercial vehicles, arguing that the measure could expose pastors and evangelists to imprisonment for sharing their faith.

The Ranking Member of Parliament for the Defence and Interior Committee said he had been preaching on commercial buses since around 2007, when he began evangelising in Tarkwa.

He questioned why the practice was now being treated as a nuisance and called on the President to direct that the regulation be abandoned.

I begun evangelizing and preaching freely in commercial buses in Tarkwa around 2007. Now they want to ban preaching in buses. I risk going to jail if I continue preaching JESUS in buses. But what shall separate me from the love of God? Shall persecution or senseless laws stop us from preaching the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ freely everywhere? Mr President, please order them to abandon this bogus regulation which seeks to jail innocent Pastors and Evangelists - simply for preaching in buses. Now preaching JESUS in buses is described as NUISANCE? Or this is also part of the unpopular policies your Ministers are pushing without your approval? Who is really in charge in this govt? We will continue to PREACH JESUS in buses, on the street, on campuses, in markets and wherever we shall find souls. We will be undeterred by these anti-preaching regulations. Thank God for the inspiration for this book which occupied my passion a few years ago -PREACHING JESUS. — John Ntim Fordjour MP (@NtimFordjour) October 8, 2026

“Mr President, please order them to abandon this bogus regulation which seeks to jail innocent Pastors and Evangelists – simply for preaching in buses,” he wrote in a social media post.

Rev. Ntim Fordjour also questioned whether the policy reflected President Mahama’s position or was being advanced by some ministers without his approval.

“Or is this also part of the unpopular policies your Ministers are pushing without your approval? Who is really in charge in this govt?” he asked.

His appeal follows the enforcement of the Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519), which prohibit preaching and hawking on public service vehicles while in motion.

The regulations prescribe a fine of between 10 and 50 penalty units, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both for offenders.

He maintained that he would continue preaching in public spaces despite the restrictions.

Ghana News.title: Volta youth farmers commend Agric Minister, appeal for markets for cassava growers
Ghana News.content:
The Volta Youth in Agriculture has congratulated the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Mr Eric Opoku, on his dedicated leadership and efforts to advance agricultural production.

The youth group, however, appealed for markets for young cassava farmers in the region.

Madam Joy Fiamawle, the Public Relations Officer of the group, in an interview, commended the Minister for his commitment to make agriculture more productive, resilient and attractive to the youth in general.

“The Minister’s emphasis on increasing food production, supporting farmers, promoting agricultural value chains and building the capacity of young people to take part meaningfully in the sector is an important step towards a stronger and more sustainable agricultural economy,” she said.

Madam Fiamawle described agriculture as more than an economic activity, and called it a powerful vehicle for job creation, youth empowerment, food security, poverty reduction and national development.

She explained that the group appreciated initiatives and policies that placed farmers and young agricultural entrepreneurs at the centre of Ghana’s development agenda.

She said: As a group, we also welcome the Minister's efforts to improve access to agricultural inputs, irrigation, mechanisation, markets, technology, and other resources needed to raise productivity.

“We believe that, with the right support, young people can become the next generation of commercial farmers, agribusiness owners, processors, exporters and agricultural innovators.”

She encouraged the Ministry to keep prioritising youth-led agriculture, particularly in regions such as the Volta, which the group said has significant potential for crop production, livestock, aquaculture, agro-processing, and agribusiness.

According to the group, a deliberate national programme that gives young farmers access to land, affordable financing, irrigation, improved seeds, mechanisation, extension services, storage and processing facilities, and guaranteed markets would significantly accelerate the transformation of the sector.

The group further suggested that stronger links between farmers and institutional buyers, including schools, hospitals, hotels, restaurants, and food processors, could create sustainable markets for locally produced commodities.

The group raised a specific concern about young cassava producers, adding that “many are becoming discouraged because they cannot find buyers for what they grow. We demand initiatives to secure markets for them.”

The Volta Youth in Agriculture assured the Minister of its willingness to work with the government and other stakeholders to promote agriculture among the youth, and pledged to continue to champion the message that agriculture is a business, a source of employment, and a pathway to prosperity.

The group said it was confident that with sustained leadership, collaboration and investment, the country could reduce its dependence on imported food, increase domestic production and build a competitive agricultural sector that could feed the nation and create wealth.

They said that the future of agriculture in the country would be brighter and that the youth must be at its heart.

Ghana News.title: Mahama commissions expanded production line at Nestlé Ghana Ltd
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday commissioned the expanded evaporated milk production line at Nestlé Ghana Limited in the industrial city of Tema.

President Mahama said Tema was a city where Ghana’s founding President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, planted the industrial ambitions of a young republic, and it remains the place where that ambition was most visibly at work.

The President noted that investment that was being commissioned retired a production line that served the factory faithfully for more than 30 years but had reached the limits of its capacity.

It is being replaced with an expanded factory production line capable of producing nearly 30,000 tons per year.

Using the newly commissioned line, President Mahama explained the government’s flagship 24-Hour Economy programme to mean “a factory that never sleeps, it works 24-7, and it supports approximately 1,200 full-time workers and about another 1,300 third-party workers.”

The President said he was happy to announce that 94.4 per cent of the employees of Nestlé were Ghanaian, saying, “this figure is most important because it shows whether a company is creating opportunities for Ghanaians as it grows its business, and to its credit, Nestlé has done that.”

“Kwame Nkrumah planned Tema as Ghana’s industrial city, and I am pleased to say that Tema is regaining its glory days. The Port of Tema has expanded. Tema Oil Refinery is back, at work again. We are working on reviving VALCO,” he said.

President Mahama said the Arise Industrial Enclave was progressing, and many industries like Nestlé existing in the Tema enclave were expanding their production.

This, he said, was because the investment climate was good; adding that foreign direct investment had risen from 624 million Ghana cedis in 2024 to 2.62 billion dollars in 2025.

“Interest rates are falling, with spreads between nine per cent and 13 per cent. Inflation, which stood at 23.8 per cent, is down to about 5.2 per cent, and our long-suffering local currency, the cedi, has regained its strength and is relatively performing very well,” he said.

To the management and staff of Nestlé Ghana Limited, President Mahama said the plant was a monument to what partnership, purpose and patriotism could achieve together.

“You belong to an institution with a proud heritage in this country and the courage to continue investing in this country’s future,” he said.

“So, keep pushing the frontiers of growth, deepen your bonds with Ghanaian farmers and suppliers, and keep creating opportunities for young people and for this nation, Ghana,” he urged.

President Mahama commended the Nestle Ghana Ltd for supporting the President’s Independence Day Award for schoolchildren for almost 30 years.

He called for continual partnership with the government as the nation and Nestle both prepared to celebrate their 70th anniversary, saying, “let today be our shared dedication, our shared declaration to the world: we are not finished, we are only starting”.

Madam Salomé Azevedo, the Managing Director of Nestlé Ghana Ltd, said the milestone the company had achieved reflected its commitment to local production and their confidence in Ghana’s very bright future.

Ghana News.title: Chief of Staff urges journalists to uphold accuracy, fairness
Ghana News.content:
The Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has urged journalists to uphold accuracy, fairness and professional ethics while using their platforms to hold public officials accountable.

He said journalists must verify information before publication, distinguish facts from allegations, respect privacy and human dignity, declare conflicts of interest and openly correct errors.

Mr Debrah made the call in Accra on Wednesday when he launched the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards and inaugurated a nine-member awards committee.

He said the media had a critical role in Ghana’s democracy and urged practitioners not to allow “the race to publish first” to compromise national peace or individuals’ rights and reputation.

“We may disagree with a headline or a conclusion, but disagreement is not hostility, and scrutiny is not disloyalty,” he said.

Mr Debrah said the rise of digital media had expanded opportunities for journalism and enabled young people to create and disseminate content without necessarily working from traditional newsrooms.

He, therefore, called on the GJA to deepen training, mentorship and engagement with digital content creators to ensure that innovation and professional ethics advanced together.

The Chief of Staff urged the awards committee, chaired by Mr Kobby Asmah, former Editor of the Graphic Communications Group, and member of the National Media Commission, to work with fairness, independence and clear standards in selecting award winners.

He said the awards should recognise journalism that was accurate, courageous, original, innovative, and useful to the public.

Mr Felix Kwakye Ofosu, the Minister in charge of Government Communications, said the Government was committed to protecting journalists and deepening the frontiers of free speech.

He condemned the recent alleged assault of journalists during a demolition exercise at the La Pleasure Beach and said the Government would pursue the matter to its logical conclusion.

Osahen Alexander Afenyo-Markin, Minority Leader of Parliament, also urged journalists to strengthen investigative reporting and pursue issues of public interest.

He said the media had a greater responsibility to seek answers when parliamentary oversight was constrained, urging journalists to “maintain absolute focus on the facts” and demand accountability.

Mr Albert Kwabena Dwumfour, GJA President, said the awards were intended to recognise journalism that informed public debate, held power to account, exposed wrongdoing and contributed to national development.

He expressed concern about recent attacks on journalists allegedly by personnel of the Ghana Armed Forces, and demanded action on the matter within two weeks.

The 30th GJA Media Awards will be held on November 7, 2026, in Accra, with President John Dramani Mahama as the Special Guest of Honour and keynote speaker.

The Speaker of Parliament and Chief Justice are also expected to attend.

The GJA said it received 327 entries from 206 journalists for this year’s awards.

Ghana News.title: Mahama pays a working visit to Three Dreamer Manufacturing
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama on Thursday paid a working visit to Three Dreamer Manufacturing Company in the industrial and port city of Tema in the Greater Accra Region.

The Company is into the manufacturing and distribution of fast-moving consumer goods such as diapers, sanitary pads, toilet rolls, non-dairy creamer, biscuits, candies, fish snacks (aborbi), beef snacks, LED bulbs and tin foods.

President Mahama in his address thanked the Management and workers of the factory for their contribution to Ghana’s industrial development.

He encouraged them to continue working hard, continue producing for Ghana and continue looking beyond Ghana to the opportunities available across the African market.

He said in the run-up to the 2024 elections, the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC) in its manifesto promised the implementation of the 24-Hour Economy.

The President said Three Dreamer Manufacturing Company was a testimony to one of the practical ways in which that policy was beginning to translate into opportunities for their people.

He said the 24-Hour Economy was not only about establishing new factories but also about supporting existing factories to expand their operations, increase production and employ more people.

He said already, existing factories were employing more people because of the opportunities being created through the 24-Hour Economy Market.

“If this factory was not here today, many of the young people we see working here would probably be at home without jobs,” he said.

He added: “This is why we must continue to support local manufacturing and create opportunities for our young people.”

President Mahama said they had the capacity to produce many of the things they consume locally; declaring that they were not only producing for the Ghanaian market and that they could also produce for export.

“Look at the tin tomatoes and light bulbs being produced here. These are products that we can manufacture locally and export to other African markets,” the President said.

He reiterated that the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) provides them with a huge opportunity to expand their production and access markets across the continent.

He said when they produce locally and export to other African countries, they create jobs for their people, generate income for businesses and strengthen their economy.

“I am particularly happy to see the enthusiasm among the young people working here. I admire how happy you are because you now have employment and an opportunity to earn a living,” President Mahama said.

He further encouraged the staff to support their employers; saying “assist your bosses to make more income so that they can expand their businesses and employ even more people”.

He said the success of a factory depends not only on the owners and management, but that the workers also had an important role to play through hard work, discipline and commitment.

President Mahama said when the business grows, the workers also benefit because the company would be able to create more opportunities and employ more people.

He said they had earlier visited Nestlé Ghana Limited, where they also witnessed the expansion of production lines and that these developments show that existing companies were responding to the opportunities in the nation’s economy by increasing their production capacity.

President Mahama said their responsibility as Government was to continue creating the right environment for businesses to produce, expand and employ more people, promising that the government would continue to pursue policies that strengthened the Ghanaian cedi and create a stable environment.

“We have seen inflation come down, and we are working to ensure that the stability of the economy is sustained. A stronger and more stable economy will provide businesses with greater confidence to invest, expand their operations and create jobs,” the President said.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Mexico prison clash in strife-torn Sinaloa state leaves 10 dead
World.content:
Nine inmates and one visitor killed in Sinaloa prison riot, local authorities say.

Ten people have been killed and 16 others injured in a fight at the El Castillo Penitentiary Centre in the city of Mazatlan, in Mexico’s northwestern state of Sinaloa, state authorities said.

The Sinaloa Public Security Secretariat said on Thursday that a fight inside the prison had left nine inmates and a family visitor dead.

Sinaloa’s Secretary of Public Security, Sinuhe Tellez, said in a video posted on social media that the visitor was a minor.

The 16 injured inmates were transferred for medical attention, the secretariat said.

An inter-institutional group of security forces moved in, and the prison is now “under control”, with authorities remaining at the site, the secretariat added.

Social work staff are contacting the families of the dead, Tellez said, noting that visits to the prison had been suspended as a precaution and the rest of the prison population was safe.

Sinaloa is a battleground for warring factions of the Sinaloa drug cartel and is one of six Mexican states the US State Department advises Americans not to visit over security concerns.

Officials have not said whether the violence at the prison was linked to that conflict.

World.title: Northern Ireland’s Sinn Fein faces police probe as protest tensions fester
World.content:
Opposition unionists call for the prosecution of Sinn Fein lawmakers who participated in the protest.

Northern Irish police have contacted representatives of Sinn Fein in an investigation into a protest that blocked a Protestant parade from marching through a Catholic area, the party said.

The Sinn Fein party leads Northern Ireland’s power-sharing government alongside its main pro-British rival, the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP), which has called for Sinn Fein lawmakers to be prosecuted.

In a statement posted to Facebook on Thursday, Sinn Fein confirmed “that a number of its representatives and party members received correspondence” from police.

“Sinn Fein will continue to stand with the Garvaghy Road residents who should be allowed to live in peace and free from sectarian intimidation,” the party said in the statement.

It added they have “stood with residents of the Garvaghy Road for the last two weeks in the face of provocation and the threat of an unwanted Orange march through their community”.

March permitted

Northern Ireland’s High Court permitted the Protestant Orange Order to march on the Catholic Garvaghy Road for the first time in 28 years.

Police opened an investigation into what they called the unlawful protest of the march, and said people reasonably suspected of committing offences will receive letters for interviews.

Sinn Fein First Minister Michelle O’Neill and Sinn Fein President Mary Lou McDonald participated in the protests.

The DUP called for O’Neill and other lawmakers to be prosecuted.

“A political title is not a shield, and no one is above the law,” the party said in a statement on Thursday.

Before the Good Friday Agreement was signed, annual attempts by the Orange Order to march through the area triggered unrest across the British-run region until the route was banned in 1998.



The standoff has become a political crisis in Northern Ireland, affecting the region’s power-sharing government.

World.title: ICE agent shoots man in car with five-year-old child in New York: Mayor
World.content:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani says agents fired at a car with a child inside; DHS says the man was an arrest target.

Share ICE agent shoots man in car with five-year-old child in New York: Mayor on social media

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent has shot a man in the Marble Hill neighbourhood of New York City, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, calling the incident an “unconscionable and incredibly serious situation”.

In a statement he published on X, Mamdani said early reports on Thursday indicated agents surrounded the man and a five-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds.

The child was believed to be physically unharmed, he added.

Mamdani said he had called President Donald Trump and would demand that he end all ICE enforcement actions in the city. “I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities,” he said.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said ICE officers were conducting a “targeted enforcement operation” in the Bronx at about 4pm to arrest a man it described as a Dominican national with a criminal conviction.

It said an officer “discharged his weapon” and the man was injured.

DHS said the incident remains under investigation.

According to a statement by the New York Police Department, the man remains conscious and is receiving medical treatment at a nearby hospital.

ICE under scrutiny

The shooting comes after months of mounting criticism of the agency.

In January, federal immigration agents shot dead two US citizens in Minneapolis: Renee Nicole Good, a 37-year-old mother of three, killed by an ICE agent on January 7, and Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care nurse, shot by a US border agent.



After Good’s killing, Trump officials labelled her a “domestic terrorist” even as video of the shooting cast doubt on claims she had tried to run over an agent.

The federal government removed local authorities from the investigation, rejected calls for a civil rights probe, and sent hundreds more agents to Minnesota, bringing the total to 3,000, as protests spread to hundreds of US cities.

Trump blamed the shift in American opinion about the immigration agency on unfair media coverage, urging DHS and ICE to publicise the “violent criminals” they arrest.

ICE has been tasked with a target of one million deportations a year.

The agency doubled in size to more than 22,000 agents by January and is now the highest-funded federal law enforcement agency, with about $75bn allocated to it over four years under a tax bill Trump signed last year.

World.title: Christa Pike case underscores prevalence of botched executions in US
World.content:
Experts say methods such as lethal injection promise more humane form of execution but are frequently marred by mishaps.

The botched execution of Christa Pike has sparked debate about the death penalty in the United States, where lethal injections, experts say, are frequently marred by mishaps and incompetence.

The attempted execution of Pike, a woman sentenced to death for her participation in the murder of a classmate when she was 18 years old, was called off after two doses of pentobarbital failed to kill her on September 30.

Witnesses reported that she continued to breathe, snore and lift parts of her body off the gurney to which she was strapped even after the lethal injections were administered. Pike’s lawyers said that she had regained consciousness at the hospital on October 6 but faces a long path to recovery.

Governor Bill Lee announced a pause on executions in the state and promised a “comprehensive, third-party review” of the incident, the second case this year in which Tennessee authorities have called off an execution after a failed lethal injection attempt.

The Tennessee Department of Correction declined to comment when asked by Al Jazeera why the execution attempt failed and whether it planned to try to execute Pike again.

While the case has attracted nationwide attention, experts say that botched execution attempts, largely carried out through lethal injection, are a disturbingly common feature of capital punishment in the US.

“This is an opportunity for everyone to stop and really carefully examine all of the ways in which this execution went wrong and to make good decisions about how to move forward, if we’re going to move forward with this method of execution,” said Robin Maher, the executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, a nonprofit research group based in Washington, DC.

Medical issues

Of the various methods of execution in the US, lethal injection is by far the most common. It is also among the least reliable.



States such as Tennessee, Idaho, Alabama, Arizona, Texas and Oklahoma have all recorded at least one botched execution via lethal injection since 2022, and a survey of executions in the US between 1890 and 2010 found that lethal injections were botched at more than twice the rate of all other methods.

Researchers attribute the poor record of lethal injection to a number of factors, including the difficulty of carrying out what amounts to a medical procedure in a prison setting without access to qualified staff.

Major medical organisations bar members from assisting in executions on the basis that it violates their mandate to do no harm, meaning that prisons rely on staff members or officials with dubious credentials to carry out the procedure.

“Lethal injection has all of the delicacies of a medical procedure: all of the error-prone qualities, all of the need for precision. But it has been warped to fit the needs of execution settings,” said Corinna Barrett Lain, a professor at the University of Richmond School of Law and author of a book on lethal injection.
